title: Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes pass data center ban
key_facts: Cheyenne and Arapaho tribal citizens voted Saturday (3 Oct 2026) for a three-year moratorium on data center construction on tribal lands.
Result: 261 for, 83 against, 7 abstentions; 351 of 478 eligible voted.
Concerns raised: water use, economics and transparency, including NDAs.
One speaker cited an estimate of 300,000 gallons of water a day for a data center.
Governor Reggie Wassanna said a data center would use a closed-loop cooling system and that the 300,000 figure was too high.
He also argued a data center could bring large income to the tribe; he said nothing has been signed and a feasibility study was planned.
quote_evidence: Cheyenne and Arapaho tribal citizens voted Saturday to impose a three-year moratorium on data center construction on tribal lands.
The final vote was 261 for the proposal, 83 against and 7 abstentions.
why_it_matters_hint: Tribal voters rejected a data center path even though their governor had argued for its benefits.
